description: Categorical-derivation probe for the (1+q)/2 multiplicative factor in Option E v9's mirror-pair closure formula. Tests 7 candidate derivation chains. Per #1581 Finding C, (1+q)/2 is empirically unique within 0.11%; this probe asks whether it is also categorically produced by the canonical chain (substrate q_0 → Hecke action → Markov trace → Frobenius pairing) rather than algebra-selected.

constraints.C1: q → 1 limit must equal 1 (classical mirror-pair collapse)
constraints.C2: at q = q_0, value must equal (1+q_0)/2 ≈ 1.054989
constraints.C3: bar-symmetry behavior consistent with mirror-pair structure
constraints.C4: arises from specific categorical object (not arbitrary algebra)

candidates.name: (a) mirror-symm crossing average
candidates.narrative: (q⁰ + q¹)/2 = (1 + q)/2 — average of vacuum and positive crossing

candidates.name: (c) Reeb phase midpoint (triv, q)
candidates.narrative: midpoint of trivial-rep χ=1 and positive-crossing χ=q on H_2(q)

candidates.name: (d) tr_M((1+σ)/2) Hoefsmit z=q
candidates.narrative: half-trace of (1 + σ) on a single Hecke strand, Hoefsmit z=q

candidates.name: (e) p-n mirror-swap projection
candidates.narrative: (σ + 1)/2 mirror-swap of one crossing to smoothing on p-n interface

candidates.name: (g) antipode-twisted (1+σ)/2
candidates.narrative: average of identity and generator: (1 + σ)/2 on positive eigenspace

chirality_factorisation.narrative: (1+q)/2 = 1 + h/2 — first-order chirality correction. NOT bar-symmetric (unlike [2]_q/2 = (q+q⁻¹)/2). The mirror-pair difference (³H − ³He) is chirality-odd by isospin parity, so the canonical operator is (1+σ)/2 (mirror-swap one crossing to smoothing) rather than (σ+σ⁻¹)/2 (bar-invariant averaging).

data.verdict: PARTIAL: candidates (b), (d), (e), (g) all give (1+q)/2 from the categorical operator (1 + σ)/2 evaluated on the symmetric eigenspace. The chain is 'use (1+σ)/2 instead of (σ+σ⁻¹)/2 because the mirror-pair difference is chirality-odd'. This is a CATEGORICAL NARRATIVE but NOT a derivation: it assumes (1+σ)/2 is the canonical averaging operator for mirror-pair differences. Bar-symmetric production code uses (σ+σ⁻¹)/2 (per cheat-sheet §5q v2). The (1+σ)/2 chirality-odd choice for the mirror-pair difference is NEW and would need separate justification.
data.open_question: Why (1+σ)/2 rather than (σ+σ⁻¹)/2 as the canonical averaging operator on the p-n interface for mirror-pair differences? The cheat-sheet §5q v2 documents (σ+σ⁻¹)/2 = σ - h/2 as the production canonical for SCALAR isotope mass; the chirality-odd (1+σ)/2 = 1 + (σ-1)/2 for ISOTOPE-PAIR DIFFERENCES is new and needs categorical justification (perhaps via Hopf antipode S(σ) = σ⁻¹ flipping the bar-symmetry under mirror swap).

proposed_categorical_chain.step_1_cat_action: σ_i → q on symmetric eigenspace V_(n)
proposed_categorical_chain.step_6_frobenius_pairing: chirality factor 1 + h/2 on antipode-twisted average
proposed_categorical_chain.discriminating_test_passed: (1+q)/2 is NOT bar-symmetric, matching the chirality-odd structure of mirror-pair difference
proposed_categorical_chain.discriminating_test_open: WHY (1+σ)/2 instead of (σ+σ⁻¹)/2 — needs Hopf-antipode justification for mirror-swap structure
